component.name: py-foliation
component.summary: Change the page labels of PDF documents
Cambiar las etiquetas de página de documentos PDF

description.p: py-foliation changes the page labels of PDF documents: the numbering a PDF viewer shows for their pages. A book whose front matter is numbered i, ii, iii and whose text starts again at 1 can show those numbers in the viewer, instead of the plain numbers of the pages of the file. Only the labels change; the pages themselves are left as they are.

py-foliation cambia las etiquetas de página de documentos PDF: la numeración que un visor de PDF muestra para sus páginas. Un libro cuyas páginas preliminares van numeradas i, ii, iii y cuyo texto empieza de nuevo en 1 puede mostrar esos números en el visor, en lugar de los números de las páginas del archivo. Solo cambian las etiquetas; las páginas quedan como están.

screenshot.caption: The ranges of labels, every page with its label, and the page chosen

description.p: A panel of thumbnails (View ▸ Thumbnails, F4), beside the preview or anywhere else in the window, whose size can be changed with a slider or Ctrl and the mouse wheel. Pages can be chosen, right-clicked and dragged there as in the list of pages, which stays a list.

Arranging pages: move, delete, duplicate, reverse and rotate them, put them in a new order, insert blank pages (as big as the page before them) or pages of another PDF, replace pages by those of another PDF, extract pages to a new file or split the document into several. The page labels follow the pages, or stay by position, as the user chooses; bookmarks and links go with their pages.
In the window, pages can be dragged in the list (with Ctrl, copied), and PDFs dropped on it insert their pages there; every change waits for Save and can be undone.

PDF/A, for archiving, and PDF/X-4, for printing: File ▸ Save as writes a copy in either standard, and so do --conform on the command line and On several files. The conversion is made by pdf2iso, which must be installed; without it those choices are greyed out.
Watermarks: a text or a page of another PDF, turned, scaled and transparent, in front of the pages or behind them, shown only when printing or only on the screen.

A page may have several headers and footers; the last one added can be updated, and the Bates numbers removed apart from the rest. Bates numbers go on from one file to the next, through several files at once, and the date has a choice of formats.
The documentation is revised; the program works as in 0.7.

Headers and footers: a left, center and right place in each, with variables such as the page label, the page number, the date or a Bates number; margins, shrinking the pages to leave room, font, color, border and background; all the pages, some, or the even or odd ones; and profiles, to use again. In the window, Pages ▸ Header and Footer and the menu of the pages, with a preview; on the command line, py-foliation header-footer. They can be removed, leaving the pages as they were.
Python 3.15 or later is needed (it was 3.13). The program is the same.
Python 3.13 or later is needed (it was 3.12). The program is the same.
No Flatpak any more, and plainer documentation and comments, in English and in Spanish. The program is the same.
The window no longer stops answering at some sizes: the scroll bars of the page preview showed and hid without end.

The initial view of the document is set from the right-click menu of the pages, or the View menu, as viewers name it: Page layout (Single, Single Continuous, Facing, Facing Continuous, Cover, Cover Continuous) and Page view (Actual Size, Fit to Width, Fit to Page). The Settings menu has Language instead of Interface Language.

Set how viewers show the document when they open it: the layout of the pages (one at a time, continuous, two side by side, the first one alone as in a book), the zoom, the panel beside the pages and the page it opens at. In the window, File ▸ View when opened…, and Open the document at this page in the menu of the pages; on the command line, py-foliation view.
Internal clean-up of the code, which is now shared between the command line and the window and split into smaller modules. The commands and the window work as before.
Choose several pages in the list and right-click them to number them, continue the numbering from before them, give them one label, or edit their labels one by one.
Folios (1r, 1v, 2r) for manuscripts and early printed books, and labels with a suffix, as [i] or 12bis.
Labels from a list, one for each page, and copied from another PDF.
Thumbnails of the pages, and going to a page by its label.
Protected PDFs keep their protection when they are saved.
The first release: the window and the command line, in English and Spanish.
